analyst_view.overall: Arsenal are 3rd in the league phase on 10 points and top of the Premier League despite Saturday's 2-2 draw at Newcastle; Dortmund are 12th on 9 points and top of the Bundesliga after a 1-0 win at Gladbach. David Raya is out with the shoulder he hurt at Newcastle (no surgery needed), so Kepa starts in goal, and Zubimendi (hamstring) and Saka (until late December) are also out; the numbers count Saka (about -10% on Arsenal's goals) but not Raya or Zubimendi. For Dortmund, Emre Can, Inácio, Konstantelias, Lerma and Kaba are out; Serhou Guirassy and Carney Chukwuemeka travelled and are available, but match-day previews (Sports Mole, ESPN, UEFA's projected XI) expect Fábio Silva to start up front with Guirassy on the bench. Kovac expects an open game. Italian referee Maurizio Mariani, slightly below average on cards, is already in the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.4 goals and already take about 10% off Arsenal for Saka. Arsenal start with their second-choice keeper Kepa instead of Raya, which the numbers don't know, while Guirassy is available for Dortmund, likely from the bench. That tilts it slightly up: 2.4 x 1.02, about 2.5.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.6 corners, with Arsenal around 6.3 and Dortmund's busier recent corner count already in (+3.0%). Arsenal build corners from sustained pressure and set pieces even without Saka, with Madueke and Eze expected wide, and Dortmund tend to defend deeper away in a back three, which both records already show, so I stay at 9.6.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.1 cards, already adding about 13% to Arsenal for their high recent card count and trimming a little for Maurizio Mariani, who averages 3.9 cards a game against a 4.1 average. There are no bans and no needle between the clubs, so nothing new points either way; I stay at 3.1.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.9 shots, with Dortmund's busy recent shooting already counted (+11.3%) and Arsenal's (+5.7%). Guirassy is back in the squad, though probably as a substitute behind Fábio Silva, while Arsenal still miss Zubimendi's control and Saka's output on the right. These roughly cancel, so I stay at 24.9.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.6 shots on target, including a small boost for Dortmund's recent accuracy (+2.7%). Guirassy, Dortmund's most clinical finisher, is available but expected on the bench after his thigh problem, and Arsenal have been less incisive without Saka, so nothing clearly moves it; I stay at 8.6.
